title: Editorial cadence and editions
summary: Publish the inaugural v0.9 desk edition and a transparent four-edition forward schedule without predating future content.
record_scope: Editorial cadence and editions records governed by the stated publication boundaries.
publication_boundaries: AI-assisted source triage can map exact artifacts and expose their limits, but it cannot stand in for the repository's required human admissibility decision.
A source-check receipt proves only that the named official artifact was inspected on the stated date; it does not admit the artifact, satisfy a requirement, or answer a mission.
No project stage, place state, comparison verdict, observation, outcome, score, rank, causal finding, recommendation, or future Phase 60 decision is created.
A repository-bounded gap says what this reviewed corpus has not established; it never asserts that qualifying evidence does not exist elsewhere.

cadence_contract.weekly: One evidence or conversion desk edition
cadence_contract.quarterly: Full mission, Atlas, comparison, freshness, accessibility, and release audit
cadence_contract.correction_rule: Material errors receive a dated correction entry; silent revision is prohibited.

editions.title: Inaugural frontier intelligence desk edition
editions.focus: All seventeen topic desks, thirty-nine Atlas files, twelve comparison re-reviews, and the open evidence-admission boundary.

editorial_sections.opening_read: The corpus is strongest as a map of institutions, projects, places, and decision requirements. It is not yet a scorecard of outcomes. This inaugural edition therefore leads with what can be traced, keeps open requirements visible, and refuses to convert source proximity into proof.
editorial_sections.evidence_admission: Six priority mission packets expose eighteen requirement-level decisions. Official artifacts were rechecked on 2026-08-30, but all admissibility decisions and mission answers remain owner-gated. Twelve additional missions still lack an exact Phase 120 topic-and-stage acquisition path.
editorial_sections.conversion_read: The Atlas carries twenty-four named project chronicles and fifteen place ledgers. Eight projects have governed Phase 61 files; sixteen remain curated. A place ledger describes its receiving system and linked projects but never inherits a synthetic project stage.
editorial_sections.longitudinal_read: All thirty-nine Atlas identities have an eligibility review. Thirty-eight have a candidate shelf and one has no repeated-record candidate shelf, but none passes the full identity, period, measure, and denominator chain required to admit a longitudinal series.
editorial_sections.comparison_read: All twelve cross-system dossiers remain Context only. Exact joins improve navigation and make boundaries inspectable; they do not establish a common stage, observation window, denominator, score, rank, or causal result.
editorial_sections.next_watch: The next lawful evidence operation is the Louisiana Starlink adoption gate on 2026-09-01. Later September and October gates remain scheduled. New editions must be written only from evidence available on or after their stated dates.

desk_dispatches.title: Advanced Manufacturing intelligence desk
desk_dispatches.current_read: This state-of-evidence review treats Advanced Manufacturing as a four-horizon research program rather than a collection of headlines. The central research problem is to distinguish installed equipment, qualified lines, receiver-accepted output and dependable production. Announced capacity and isolated delivery milestones are useful chronology, but neither supplies a stable account of yield, rework, downtime, workforce qualification or customer acceptance. The workbench currently contains 3 missions with exact Phase 120 packet joins and 1 with an acquisition-coverage gap. That split describes preparation, not truth or importance: all four missions remain unadjudicated. The review reads the evidence in the inherited Phase 124 order, connects it to 4 exact Phase 125 annotations and 4 source identities, and preserves each Phase 126 requirement test. Its purpose is to show what the corpus can orient, where definitions or denominators break, and which exact record would most improve the next review. Readers can use this review to see why production announcements and industrial-policy totals should not be mistaken for dependable capacity. It also identifies where official program records support a bounded statement and where only a company or program-level account is available.
